beats.visual: Thick white vapor pouring from a tailpipe in cold backlit morning sun, dark asphalt behind, the plume curling slowly and not thinning, no people
beats.narration: White exhaust smoke long after warmup.

beats.visual: An oil filler cap lifted and resting on a steel bench, tan milky sludge coating its underside, macro, hard side light, smooth unmarked cap
beats.narration: Milky film under the oil cap can point to coolant.

beats.visual: A head gasket laid flat on a clean steel bench, metal fire rings and coolant ports catching a low raking light, shallow depth of field
beats.narration: One thin gasket keeps coolant and combustion apart.

beats.visual: Colored coolant inside a smooth unmarked translucent reservoir with fine bubbles rising steadily through it, dim engine bay behind, shallow focus
beats.narration: Bubbles in the tank, plus a sweet smell.

beats.visual: The same tailpipe in the same cold backlit morning sun, dark asphalt behind, only a faint clear shimmer of exhaust rising now where the thick white plume had been
beats.narration: Do not guess on one clue.

ig_fb_copy.primaryCaption: White smoke from your tailpipe that doesn't clear after a minute? Check your oil cap — if it looks like a milkshake instead of black oil, that's coolant mixing in. One clue alone doesn't confirm it, but both together are worth a look. Stop by and we'll take a look.

adVariants.caption: Persistent white smoke plus a milky oil cap can point to coolant and oil mixing where they shouldn't. Two clues, one quick check.
